title: RT-2: Vision-Language-Action Models Transfer Web Knowledge to Robotic Control
grouping: Three tall light-grey outlined rounded panels side by side, each titled by a grey sans heading set into a gap in its top border: 'Internet-Scale VQA + Robot Action Data' (left), 'Vision-Language-Action Models for Robot Control' (wide middle), 'Closed-Loop Robot Control' (narrow right). The left panel stacks three white rounded cards, each a photo plus a Q:/A: example; the third is a robot-camera frame whose answer is the action. Inside the middle panel a large grey rounded box named RT-2 holds a blue ViT box and an orange-tinted 'Large Language Model' panel. The panels are joined only by two grey elbow arrows along the bottom edge labelled 'Co-Fine-Tune' and 'Deploy'. Colour families: orange for the question text and the <task> slot, blue for the vision encoder, purple for answers and actions.
shapes_depth: Flat rounded rectangles with thin outlines, no shadows. Tokens are small horizontal pills: an orange-outlined row for the prompt, a row of blue/orange/grey pills entering and leaving one wide orange-outlined LLM bar, the last three output pills purple and gathered by a purple curly brace. The visual input is a 3x3 grid of robot-camera frames fed by a grey arrow into ViT. The numeric answer strings ('A: 311 423 170 55 244', 'A: 132 114 128 5 25 156') are set in light grey, and short curved purple arrows lead from each to a purple-filled answer box; for the robot example the box holds 'ΔTranslation = [0.1, -0.2, 0]' and 'ΔRotation = [10°, 25°, -7°]'. The right panel stacks three robot photos with translucent white curved arrows painted over the motion and a white caption strip with the instruction under each.
proposed_highlight: The model name RT-2 is the largest, boldest dark-grey text, set in the corner of its own grey box. The action path is the only saturated thread: purple output tokens under a brace -> purple elbow to an 'A: 132 114 ...' box -> purple 'De-Tokenize' label -> purple 'Robot Action' box with ΔT and ΔR, the same purple as the answer boxes of the web-data examples.
lesson: Give robot actions the same colour as the text answers in the training-data examples (purple boxes) and carry that colour along the output tokens -> de-tokenize -> ΔT/ΔR box, so 'actions are just another answer' reads without a word.
notes: Venue CoRL from Semantic Scholar (title match, venue_source: semantic-scholar); year 2023 = S2 year and arXiv year. Photos and camera frames are embedded rasters recorded by refs crop.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

core.what: three titled rounded frames left to right - training data, the RT-2 vision-language-action model, closed-loop robot control - joined by grey 'Co-Fine-Tune' and 'Deploy' arrows along the bottom

relations.form: left data frame -> 'Co-Fine-Tune' arrow up into the centre model frame -> 'Deploy' arrow down-right into the right frame of robot photos with instructions

the left frame stacks three identical Q/A cards (English VQA, French VQA, a robot <task>), each with a grey token-number answer and a purple decoded answer, so robot actions share the text-answer format
orange text-token pills from the prompt and blue image tokens from the ViT (fed a 3x3 grid of robot frames) enter one orange 'Large Language Model' panel
output tokens under the LLM are bracketed and routed down to 'A: 132 114 ...', then 'De-Tokenize' to ΔT/ΔR in a 'Robot Action' box

channels.colour: orange = text tokens and the LLM (and the <task> placeholder), blue = image tokens and ViT, purple = answers/action tokens and the decoded action; grey = token-number strings and pipeline arrows
channels.shape: pills = tokens, rounded rectangles = models and answers, photos = observations
channels.line: solid grey arrows for stage transitions and data, purple line for the action-token path
channels.frame: three outlined rounded frames = data / model / deployment stages; tinted inner panels = model components

quality.strengths: the key idea - actions written as text answers - is visible because the robot card has the same form and purple answer box as the two VQA cards; tokens are drawn as coloured pills so the image and text inputs to the LLM are seen as data; the action is shown as real numbers and real robot photos
quality.weaknesses: the LLM is a single empty bar between two token rows; the purple action path loops out of the model frame and back in to reach 'De-Tokenize'; orange marks both text tokens and the whole LLM panel; the co-fine-tuning mixture is not drawn beyond the three example cards

insights.structure: Three grey-outlined rounded panels side by side with titles set into their top border: data examples (left), the RT-2 model (wide middle, a grey box holding a blue ViT and an orange Large Language Model panel), and closed-loop control photos (narrow right).
insights.data: Training data are photo cards with Q:/A: text and a grey token-number answer, the visual input is a 3x3 grid of robot camera frames, tokens are small pill rows, and actions are written as ΔT/ΔR vectors in purple boxes.
insights.emphasis: Actions are drawn in the same purple as the text answers of web VQA examples, and the purple thread runs from braced output tokens through 'De-Tokenize' to a 'Robot Action' box, with 'RT-2' as the largest bold text.
insights.flow: Panels are connected only by two grey elbow arrows along the bottom ('Co-Fine-Tune', 'Deploy'); inside the middle panel the prompt and images enter from the left, rise through the LLM, and output exits down via a purple elbow.
insights.avoid: The token-number answers in light grey ('A: 311 423 ...') are nearly invisible against white; the 3x3 robot frame grid is too small to read.

arrangement.units: three tall rounded outline panels left to right (data, model, deployment), each titled in grey text inset into its top border
arrangement.inputs_as: white cards each pairing a real photo with a Q:/A: example
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; training is the 'Co-Fine-Tune' arrow label along the bottom
arrangement.shared: purple answer/action boxes recur in the data panel and the model panel
